name: Pagani Zonda F
description: The Pagani Zonda F (or Zonda Fangio, named after Formula One legend Juan Manuel Fangio) debuted at the 2005 Geneva Motor Show as the most extensively re-engineered variant of the Zonda lineup. At its heart is a 7.3-liter Mercedes-AMG M297 V12 engine producing 602 hp at 6,150 rpm and 760 Nm of torque at 4,000 rpm, achieved through enhanced intake manifolds, revised exhaust, and an updated ECU. The transmission features strengthened internals and differential gears, enabling a top speed of 345 km/h. Production was limited to just 25 cars. The Zonda F features revised bodywork including a new front end, rear spoiler, and enhanced aerodynamic vents, along with optional 380mm carbon-ceramic Brembo brakes, OZ alloy wheels, an Inconel exhaust system, and a hydroformed aluminum intake plenum. The redesigned carbon fiber crash structure uses Pagani's signature 'Z-preg' weave for improved rigidity and reduced weight, resulting in a curb weight of just 1,275 kg.
